title: Unified connection lifecycle and idempotent replay spec for SDKs (Py/TS/Go)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: PRD to define a common connection lifecycle and idempotent replay model across Redwood SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go) to improve streaming reliability, support safe client downgrades, and enable server-side rolling upgrades without data loss or duplication.
background: Customers using long-lived streaming connections (chat, embeddings streaming, real-time inference) report inconsistent behavior during network flaps and during server-side rollouts: duplicate events, partial responses, and opaque reconnection semantics. SDKs currently implement ad-hoc reconnect and retry logic per language which complicates cross-team rollouts and causes subtle incompatibilities with older runtime versions. This spec standardizes connection state, replay tokens, cursor semantics for pagination, and a minimal backpressure API to make rollouts, downgrades, and client-side retries safer.
scope:
- Define connection lifecycle states (connected, paused, reconnecting, tombstoned) and observable hooks in SDKs
- Specify idempotent replay token format and minimal server guarantees
- Define hybrid pagination + streaming cursor semantics for resuming large result sets
- Backpressure API for consumer-level flow control (per-language ergonomic surface)
- Cross-SDK compatibility rules and graceful downgrade behavior
- Acceptance criteria and interop tests for runtime compatibility matrix
out_of_scope:
- Server implementation details beyond minimal guarantees described here
- Full automatic state migration tools for customer on-prem deployments
- Language-specific syntactic sugar beyond ergonomic examples
requirements: 1) Connection lifecycle: SDK must surface deterministic lifecycle events and expose an opt-in auto-reconnect with configurable backoff and fastpath replay
2) Replay tokens: Server issues an opaque replay_token at stable checkpoints; SDK uses token to request replay from a resume point; replay must be idempotent
3) Cursor semantics: For paginated streaming results, SDKs should expose a combined cursor model (cursor+offset) to support both stateless pagination and resumable streams
4) Backpressure: Provide a minimal API to pause/resume consumption and expose buffered bytes/messages; default implementations must be safe for web/browser (TS) and long-running processes (Py/Go)
5) Retry policies: Standardize default retry for transient errors (network 5xx, connection reset) with Jittered exponential backoff and a maximum time window configurable per SDK
6) Idempotency keys: In addition to replay tokens, SDK should surface optional per-request idempotency keys to support non-streaming idempotent operations
7) Compatibility: Clients must detect server capability headers and gracefully degrade features (e.g., omit replay requests if server does not advertise resume capability)
8) Observability: SDKs must emit structured telemetry hooks (events) for lifecycle transitions, replay attempts, and discarded buffers to aid debugging
9) Test suite: Provide cross-language interop test scenarios validating replay correctness, duplicate suppression, and downgrade behavior
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (Py/TS/Go) implement lifecycle API exposing at minimum: on_connect, on_disconnect, on_replay_start, on_replay_end, on_tombstone
Replay token roundtrip: create stream -> obtain token -> simulate disconnect -> resume using token -> result state equals sequential full stream (no duplicates) in 95% interop test runs
Pagination/resume: Resuming mid-page using cursor+offset returns deterministic continuation without skipping or duplicating items
Downgrade safety: Client talking to server that does NOT support replay will not attempt replay and instead falls back to last-successful semantics without raising unrecoverable errors
Backward compatibility: Older SDK versions should still function (best-effort) with new server rollouts; new SDKs must detect legacy servers and restrict advanced features
Observability: Telemetry events include timestamp, lifecycle_state, replay_token (redacted), and retry_count for every reconnection path
Performance: Default auto-reconnect/backoff does not increase median latency for non-reconnect paths by more than 3% in synthetic benchmarks
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Spec review and design doc + reference implementation in Python (2 weeks)
Phase 2: Implement TS and Go SDK updates and add interop test harness (3 weeks)
Phase 3: Canary runtime rollout with resume-capable endpoints; run interop tests across canary hosts (2 weeks)
Phase 4: Gradual global rollout and monitor replay error rates and customer impact (4 weeks)
Fallback: If replay-related error rate increases >0.5% during rollout, disable resume capability at runtime and roll back clients to conservative behavior
migration_notes: Clients should adopt new lifecycle hooks incrementally. Provide a compatibility shim for existing call sites: default to legacy behavior unless opt-in flag enable_resume=true is set. Document sample migration path for customers with long-lived sessions.
open_questions: Q1: Should replay_token be opaque binary or structured (versioned JSON)? Trade-offs: opaqueness simplifies server evolution, structured tokens simplify client validation.
Q2: What is the maximum retention window for server-side resume checkpoints? (30s/5m/1h tradeoffs with storage cost)
Q3: How should SDKs surface partial replay failure to caller semantics (exceptions vs. resumable error objects)?
Q4: Browser TS constraints: are background reconnects allowed when tab is suspended?
decisions: D1: Use opaque, base64-encoded replay_token with server-side version header to enable evolution
D2: Default resume window set to 5 minutes for Hosted and Dedicated; on-prem customers can configure via server setting
D3: SDKs will surface replay failure as an explicit lifecycle event and a recoverable error object; they will not throw by default unless user opts into strict mode
D4: Backpressure API will be minimal: pause(), resume(), buffered_count() across languages with language-specific ergonomic wrappers
